prompt: A train takes a banked curve faster than the designed speed. The extra centripetal force comes from the
options: Outer rail pushing inward on the flange
explain: The outer rail's flange thrust is directed inward, so the outer rail wears.

subject: Physics
prompt: For the same μ and r, the maximum safe speed on a banked road compared with a flat road is
explain: v_max² = rg(tanθ+μ)/(1−μtanθ) > μrg, because the normal reaction also contributes.

subject: Physics
prompt: On a frictionless banked road, the net force on a car of mass m at the ideal speed is
explain: N sinθ = mg tanθ, directed horizontally toward the centre; it equals mv²/r.

subject: Physics
prompt: A car is at rest on a banked road with μ < tanθ. It will
options: Slide only if mass is large
explain: Limiting friction μmg cosθ < mg sinθ when μ < tanθ, so it slides down, independent of mass.

subject: Physics
prompt: A car moves at constant speed on a level circular road. Net friction on it is directed:
explain: Static friction is the only horizontal force, so it points to the centre and supplies the centripetal force.

subject: Physics
prompt: A car speeds up while on a level circular bend. The friction on it points:
explain: Friction supplies a radial part mv²/r and a forward tangential part ma_t.

subject: Physics
prompt: Cars of mass m and 2m take the same level bend at the same speed without skidding. Friction ratio is:
explain: Required friction mv²/r is proportional to mass at fixed v and r, so the ratio is 1 : 2.

subject: Physics
prompt: A car turns at high speed on a level bend. Compared with the inner wheels, the normal reaction on the outer wheels is:
explain: The torque of friction about the CM shifts the load outward, so the outer wheels carry more normal reaction.

subject: Physics
prompt: On a frictionless banked road, a car at more than the ideal speed will
options: Move steadily on the same path
Skid up the slope toward the outer edge
Slip down toward the inner edge
explain: N sinθ is too small for the required centripetal force, so the car drifts outward and up the slope.

subject: Physics
prompt: A train takes a banked curve slower than the designed speed. The extra lateral force comes from the
options: Inner rail pushing inward on the flange
Outer rail pushing outward on the flange
Outer rail pushing inward on the flange
Inner rail pushing outward on the flange
explain: At low speed the train tends to slide inward, so the inner rail's flange pushes it outward, away from the centre.

subject: Physics
prompt: Two bodies of masses 1 kg and 9 kg have equal momentum. Ratio of KE (lighter : heavier) is:
explain: For equal p, K ∝ 1/m, so the lighter body has 9 times the KE.

subject: Physics
prompt: The KE of a body of fixed mass increases by 44%. Its momentum increases by:
explain: p ∝ √K, and √1.44 = 1.2, so p rises by 20%.

subject: Physics
prompt: Bodies of different masses with equal momentum are stopped by the same constant retarding force. What is equal?
explain: F t = p, so equal p and equal F give equal time. Distance and deceleration differ.

subject: Physics
prompt: Bodies of different masses with equal KE are stopped by the same constant retarding force. What is equal?
explain: By the work–energy theorem, F s = K, so equal K and equal F give equal distance.

subject: Physics
prompt: A water jet (ρ, A, v) strikes a wall and rebounds with the same speed. Force on the wall is:
explain: Δp per kg is 2v for a rebound, so F = (ρAv)(2v) = 2ρAv².

subject: Physics
prompt: For a projectile in vacuum, the rate of change of its momentum is:
explain: Only gravity acts, so dp/dt = mg downward. Horizontal momentum stays constant.

subject: Physics
prompt: In a very short collision, which force is neglected compared with the impulsive force?
explain: Impulsive force is very large over a tiny time; finite forces such as weight give negligible impulse then.

subject: Physics
prompt: Equal impulse acts on bodies of mass m and 4m, both at rest. Ratio of KE gained (lighter : heavier)?
explain: Same impulse gives same p, so K ∝ 1/m; the lighter body gains 4 times more KE.

subject: Physics
prompt: Force rises linearly from 0 to F₀ in time T on a body, then stops. Impulse delivered is:
explain: Impulse is the area under the F–t graph, a triangle: ½ × T × F₀.

subject: Physics
prompt: A ball of mass m thrown up with speed u returns to the hand. Impulse of gravity over the flight?
explain: Δp = (−mu) − (+mu) = −2mu, i.e. 2mu downward (also mg·2u/g).

subject: Physics
prompt: A ball hits a smooth wall obliquely and rebounds elastically. Impulse on the ball is directed:
options: Along the normal to the wall
explain: Smooth wall gives no tangential force, so only the normal momentum component changes.

subject: Physics
prompt: While you walk forward, the force that pushes you ahead is:
options: Your foot's push on the ground
Friction by ground on your foot
explain: Foot pushes ground backward (action); ground's static friction on foot, forward, is the reaction.

subject: Physics
prompt: For a book resting on a table, which is a genuine action-reaction pair?
options: Weight of book and normal force on book
Normal force on book and book's push on table
Weight of book and book's push on table
Normal force on book and Earth's pull on table
explain: Table pushes book up, book pushes table down: same nature, different bodies. Weight and N act on the same body.

subject: Physics
prompt: An apple falls; Earth pulls it with F, so apple pulls Earth with F. Earth's acceleration is negligible because:
options: Earth's reaction acts after a delay
Gravity acts only on the apple
Force on Earth is much smaller
explain: Forces are equal in magnitude; a = F/M is tiny for Earth's huge mass.

subject: Physics
prompt: In a 1D elastic collision, relative speed of separation compared with relative speed of approach is:
explain: Elastic collision has e = 1, so separation speed equals approach speed.

subject: Physics
prompt: Two blocks with a spring between them collide. At maximum compression, the two blocks have:
explain: At maximum compression, both move with the same common velocity.

subject: Physics
prompt: A light ball hits a much heavier ball at rest elastically with speed v. The light ball:
explain: For m₁ ≪ m₂, v₁′ ≈ −v, just like a rigid wall.

subject: Physics
topic: Pseudo force, apparent weight in lift
prompt: A block stays at rest on a smooth wedge of angle θ that accelerates horizontally. The wedge's acceleration is:
formula: N sinθ = ma, N cosθ = mg
explain: In the wedge frame, the pseudo force ma, mg and N balance. This gives tanθ = a/g, so a = g tanθ.

subject: Physics
topic: Angle of friction, angle of repose
prompt: While a block slides on a rough surface, its contact force makes what angle with the normal?
explain: Kinetic friction is μₖN, so the contact force is inclined at tan⁻¹μₖ, which is less than λ because μₖ < μₛ.

subject: Physics
prompt: Centripetal force in terms of linear momentum p of the particle (mass m, radius r) is:
explain: F = mv²/r with v = p/m gives p²/(mr).

subject: Physics
prompt: At constant speed v, the centripetal force on a given mass varies with radius r as:
explain: With v fixed, F = mv²/r ∝ 1/r, whereas at fixed ω it would be ∝ r.

subject: Physics
prompt: A particle moves in a circle with increasing speed. Its net acceleration points:
options: Inclined between the radius and tangent
explain: It has a radial part v²/r and a tangential part dv/dt, so the net acceleration does not point to the centre.

subject: Physics
prompt: At speed v on a level road, the minimum turning radius compared with the minimum straight stopping distance is:
explain: r_min = v²/(μg) is twice s_min = v²/(2μg), so braking straight is safer.

subject: Physics
prompt: A cyclist leans at angle θ to the vertical on a level curve without slipping. The minimum μ needed is:
explain: f/N = (mv²/r)/mg = tanθ, and this must not exceed μ.

subject: Physics
prompt: At maximum safe speed on a rough banked road, the normal reaction N compared with that at ideal speed is
explain: Friction down the slope has a downward vertical part, so N cosθ = mg + μN sinθ gives larger N.

subject: Physics
prompt: The main advantage of banking a curved road is that it
options: Reduces dependence on friction and tyre wear
Makes the ideal speed independent of radius
Reduces the radius of the turn
explain: The normal reaction's horizontal component supplies part or all of the centripetal force, so less friction is needed.

subject: Physics
prompt: On a frictionless banked road, a car moving slower than the ideal speed will:
options: Skid up toward the outer edge
Slide down toward the inner edge
explain: N sinθ exceeds the needed mv²/r, so the car slides down the slope.

subject: Physics
prompt: A cyclist leans on a turn. The resultant of normal reaction and friction at the ground passes through the:
options: Centre of mass of cyclist plus cycle
explain: For rotational balance, the resultant ground force passes through the centre of mass, so the lean angle follows tanθ = v²/rg.
